name: Bishlam
title: Persian official in Samaria
summary: Bishlam was one of the Persian officials or settlers in Samaria who wrote a letter of complaint to King Artaxerxes of Persia to stop the rebuilding of Jerusalem. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Ezra 4:7, as one of the co-authors of the letter. His actions represent the opposition the Jews faced when they returned from exile to rebuild their city and temple.

keyEvents.title: Letter of Complaint to King Artaxerxes
keyEvents.description: Bishlam, together with Mithredath, Tabeel and other associates, wrote a letter to the Persian king Artaxerxes complaining about the Jews' rebuilding of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The Accusations Against Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: The letter claimed that Jerusalem had historically been a rebellious and wicked city, and that its rebuilding would lead the Jews to stop paying taxes and tribute to the Persian Empire.

keyEvents.title: The King's Response and Work Stopped
keyEvents.description: As a result of the letter, King Artaxerxes investigated the matter and ordered that the rebuilding of Jerusalem be halted by force, which was a temporary victory for the opponents.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to God's People
keyEvents.description: Bishlam's actions were part of broader opposition exerted by the people of Samaria and Persian officials against the return and rebuilding of the Jewish people, an opposition that had already begun during the reign of Cyrus.
